Chargedst
CHAR-jed-st
v.
From Old French chargier (to load, to burden, to command), from Latin carricare; the archaic second-person singular past tense ("thou chargedst") appearing once in the Authorized Version, in Moses' recollection of the giving of the law at Sinai.

Biblical Definition

For thou chargedst us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.

Chargedst appears once in the Authorized Version, in Moses' words to the LORD at Sinai, recalling the specific command God had given: set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it (Exo 19:23), a boundary marking the mountain as too holy for the people to approach on pain of death, as the LORD had already warned whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death (Exo 19:12). The exchange in Exodus 19 shows Moses actively engaging with God's instructions, going up and down the mountain repeatedly to relay warnings and receive clarifications, careful that the people not break through unto the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish (Exo 19:21). The bounded mountain, smoking, quaking, and thundering as the LORD descended upon it in fire, stands as one of Scripture's most vivid pictures of the terror proper to an unmediated approach to a holy God under the law, a terror the author of Hebrews later contrasts directly with the access believers now have: ye are not come unto the mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire... but ye are come unto mount Sion (Heb 12:18, 22). The bounds Moses was charged to set were themselves a mercy, protecting a sinful people from a holiness they could not otherwise survive approaching.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828), from CHARGE: to command; to lay an injunction upon; the archaic second-person singular past tense here of God's command to bound off Sinai from the people.

expand to see more

CHARGE, v.t. To command; to enjoin; to lay a duty or task upon.

CHARGEDST, v. Archaic second-person singular past tense: thou didst command.

In Exodus 19:23 the word recalls God's command to set bounds around Mount Sinai.

The bounds protected the people, who could not survive an unmediated approach to God's holiness.

Hebrews 12:18-22 contrasts this terror with the believer's now-open access to 'mount Sion.'

Key Scripture

Exo 19:23 — "And Moses said unto the LORD, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou chargedst us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it."

Modern Corruption

A casual approach to God that treats access to Him as automatic and without cost misses what the bounded mountain teaches about the holiness sin makes dangerous to approach apart from a mediator.

expand to see more

A therapeutic religious culture that assumes God is simply, always approachable without qualification can lose the weight this scene carries: even Moses, God's own chosen mediator, had to relay careful bounds to protect the people from a holiness that would otherwise have consumed them.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is Hebrews' own comparison: the terror of Sinai's bounded mountain has been replaced, not by casualness, but by the far greater access purchased through Christ's blood, which speaketh better things than that of Abel (Heb 12:24).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Chargedst occurs once, in Moses' recollection of God's command to bound off Mount Sinai, a mercy protecting sinful Israel from a holiness they could not survive approaching, later contrasted with the believer's access through Christ.

expand to see more

Chargedst in Exodus 19:23 recalls God's command to 'set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.'

Exodus 19:12 explains the stakes: 'whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death.'

Moses relayed the command carefully, going up and down the mountain repeatedly (Exo 19:21).

Hebrews 12:18-22 names the same mountain 'that might be touched, and that burned with fire.'

Hebrews 12:24 contrasts this with Christ's blood, which 'speaketh better things than that of Abel.'

Usage

"For thou chargedst us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it."

"Whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death (Exo 19:12)."

"Ye are come unto mount Sion... to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant (Heb 12:22, 24)."
